transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood Solutions Eng); Jordan Blake (Ignition Lead ML Eng), Priya Rao (Ignition CTO), Evan Morales (Ignition Infra), Tasha Kim (Ignition Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping session to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing for benchmarking, and decision criteria across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment modes. Primary concerns: data residency/PII, predictable latency, burn rate (query volume), and timeline for a 4-6 week pilot.

Topics:
- Success criteria and acceptance tests
- Workload sizing: concurrency, token distribution, request patterns
- Benchmark plan and tooling
- Tradeoffs: latency vs cost, canary/rollout plan, security requirements (KMS/SSO/SOC2)
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: okay hi everyone thanks for making time, this is Ava from Redwood, joining from SF. um quick intro, Samir is our SE, Maya will help with the pilot runbook. Jordan, Priya, thanks for scheduling.
[00:12] Jordan Blake: thanks, yes, trying to keep this tight we have a lot to cover — will be heavy on the infra constraints.
[00:18] Priya Rao: hi all, short note — we need to be mindful of PCI/PII because some psi-like tokens might surface in the prompts.
[00:26] Evan Morales: yep network control is key, can't open arbitrary egress to public endpoints without our security team's sign-off.
[00:33] Samir Chen: understood, we can scope private deployment options or VPC-hosted Redwood Private. but first let's baseline what success looks like for the POC.
[00:43] Tasha Kim: product-wise we want latency under 350ms p95 for single-turn text generation and throughput to support up to 200 concurrent sessions during peak.
[00:53] Ava Martinez: okay p95 350ms and concurrency 200 noted. is that for the final prod target or pilot?
[00:58] Tasha Kim: for pilot we'd like to simulate peak traffic as acceptance criteria, so yes that should be part of the benchmark.
[01:07] Jordan Blake: and we need token-level cost visibility — our finance team wants an estimate of cost per 1M tokens and burn rate so we can model run-rate.
[01:15] Samir Chen: we can provide a cost breakdown across hosted, dedicated and private. usually hosted is fastest to stand up and cheaper at low volume, dedicated gives predictable throughput and better per-token price once committed, private is higher setup cost but required when egress or data residency blocks hosted.
[01:28] Priya Rao: our legal will require SOC2 attestation and audit logs, and key management integration — we run keys in-house (HSM). is that supported?
[01:36] Ava Martinez: yes Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations; for Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key via KMS and audit logs via the Console. hosted has managed keys but we can discuss enterprise options.
[01:48] Evan Morales: what about model variants and quantization? we may want 8-bit quant to save cost, but worried about quality.
[01:55] Samir Chen: good question — Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles per workload. for the benchmark we can test baseline fp16, 8-bit int8, and a quantized variant to measure quality delta and tokens/sec.
[02:07] Maya Lopez: also we should test prefix/KV cache hit scenarios because many of Ignition's prompts reuse context; that can dramatically reduce cost and latency.
[02:15] Jordan Blake: yes our main workload is multi-turn customer support summarization, so KV cache hit-rate will be high. we can provide sample convo traces.
[02:23] Ava Martinez: perfect. for the benchmark plan I propose: 1) customer provides 3 prompt sets (short single-turn, multi-turn medium, heavy multi-turn with 4-6 steps) 2) Redwood runs a benchmark harness simulating concurrency profiles and varying seq lengths 3) measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, NVidia GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens for each deployment mode.
[02:42] Priya Rao: timeline? we'd like results within two weeks of providing data.
[02:46] Samir Chen: realistic timeline is 10 business days to configure and run the first set of bench marks if we get artifacts quickly. pilot runbook for a 4-6 week POC after that.
[02:55] Tasha Kim: acceptance criteria beyond latency/throughput — model quality: rouge/bleu or custom cbx evaluation?
[03:02] Jordan Blake: we'll have an internal eval set and human quality checks; threshold is 92% of current baseline scoring on our eval set.
[03:09] Ava Martinez: noted — we'll include quality regression checks in the benchmark report.
[03:13] Evan Morales: network: for Private we need to know if Redwood can support air-gapped setup for an on-prem appliance.
[03:20] Samir Chen: Redwood Private has an on-prem package option, but that raises setup time — usually 4-6 weeks for on-prem provisioning. for VPC-hosted we can do a faster onramp with customer VPC peering and restricted egress in 2 weeks.
[03:33] Priya Rao: and SLA? Dedicated gives better latency SLAs?
[03:36] Ava Martinez: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and tail latency targets for committed capacity. hosted has standard shared infra SLAs but no reserved GPUs.
[03:46] Jordan Blake: cost question — how does reserved capacity pricing compare to hosted burst pricing?
[03:50] Samir Chen: short answer: hosted is pay-as-you-go; reserved (Dedicated) gives a discount in exchange for monthly commit. we'll send a model, but rough example — once you exceed ~X tokens/month reserved tends to be cheaper. (note: specific numbers to be included in cost sheet).
[04:06] Tasha Kim: can we do a hybrid? start hosted for immediate dev and then switch to dedicated when we cross threshold?
[04:11] Maya Lopez: yes, Redwood supports rolling to a dedicated pool and routing policies to fall back to hosted if capacity shortfalls occur. we can set canary rollouts and automatic fallback.
[04:20] Jordan Blake: important — we need deterministic failover behavior; if dedicated saturates, we don't want silent latency spikes.
[04:26] Samir Chen: we'll outline routing policies and circuit-breaker rules in the runbook. can also do traffic shadowing during the switch.
[04:32] Ava Martinez: okay next vis-a-vis benchmarks: what concurrency distribution should we simulate?
[04:36] Jordan Blake: peak 200 concurrent, 95% of requests are sub-512 tokens, 5% long contexts up to 4k tokens. burstiness 3x baseline lasting ~5 minutes.
[04:47] Evan Morales: encryption at rest and in transit is must. we also need per-request audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[04:53] Samir Chen: supported — audit logs to S3, CloudWatch, or push to SIEM via webhook.
[04:58] Priya Rao: on regulatory footprint, data residency: we need EU-only model hosting for certain cohorts. is that possible on Hosted?
[05:05] Ava Martinez: Hosted has region options; for strict EU-only customers we recommend Dedicated in a EU region or Private deployment inside their EU VPC.
[05:12] Tasha Kim: demo request — can Redwood show throughput numbers for a similar customer?
[05:16] Samir Chen: yes I'll pull anonymized benchmark slides and a sample harness.
[05:20] Jordan Blake: who will own running the bench marks? Redwood or Ignition?
[05:24] Ava Martinez: Redwood will run the initial bench marks if Ignition provides datasets and access patterns. then we can hand over the harness so Ignition can run repeatable tests in their environment.
[05:33] Priya Rao: what's the rollback story if we see quality regression on quantized models?
[05:38] Maya Lopez: rollback is model-version controlled; rollout policies let us revert to previous variant automatically if quality thresholds aren't met.
[05:44] Evan Morales: for Private/on-prem, who handles updates and security patches?
[05:49] Samir Chen: we have an on-prem ops pack where we push signed updates; can be managed by Redwood or turned over to the customer.
[05:56] Jordan Blake: SLA for support during pilot? we need a fast path for Sev1.
[05:59] Ava Martinez: enterprise pilot comes with a dedicated CSM and a specified on-call for Sev1 triage. we'll document response times.
[06:07] Tasha Kim: ok, let's recap acceptance criteria so we are aligned:\n- Performance: p95 single-turn generation < 350ms (pilot simulated peak)\n- Throughput: support 200 concurrent sessions with 3x burst for short windows\n- Quality: >=92% of current baseline on internal eval set\n- Security: SOC2 or equivalent, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs to SIEM, EU residency for cohort A\n- Cost: rough per-1M token model and projected month-to-month burn estimate for pilot\n[06:35] Ava Martinez: great recap. next steps are in the action items. I'll send the cost model and a proposed bench harness by Monday (2026-02-16). Samir will send the runbook and sample harness repo.
[06:47] Jordan Blake: we'll aim to deliver prompt sets and redacted logs by Wednesday (2026-02-18).
[06:52] Priya Rao: one last Q — any hidden ops work for Dedicated capacity? like networking or VPNs we should budget for?
[06:59] Samir Chen: Dedicated requires some network configuration, likely peering and security groups. Private on-prem can require additional ops time. we'll call out those items in the runbook.
[07:07] Tasha Kim: ok that works. thanks everyone.
[07:10] Ava Martinez: thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet, cost sheet, and bench harness links.

End of meeting.
